issues.description: Loop invariant / data shape for `args` is not stated; offset arithmetic invites off-by-one regressions.
issues.detail: The fix relies on the invariant that after filtering to word/function nodes, position 0 is `from`, position 1 is the source color, and positions 2..N are the channels. That invariant is load-bearing but uncommented. A one-line literate comment naming the positions would let a reader verify correctness without running the test suite.

issues.description: Nested relative-color forms (e.g., `oklch(from hsl(...) l c h)`) are not analyzed for correctness of the offset.
issues.detail: When the source color is itself a function (`oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)`), `args[1]` is a function node, not a word. The filter keeps functions, so the offset still lands on the right channel, but this case deserves an explicit invariant statement and a comment, since a future refactor that drops `function` from the filter would silently break it.

issues.description: `0 + offset` is dead arithmetic; reads as a leftover from mechanical editing.
issues.detail: `args[0 + offset]` should be `args[offset]`. The compiler folds it, but a careful reader pauses on it. Small, but in a rule file that will be read many more times than written, the cleaner form is preferable.

issues.description: `isRelativeColor` detection trusts `args[0]` shape without guarding non-word first args.
issues.detail: `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() === 'from'` is safe when `args[0]` exists and has a string `value`, which the word/function filter guarantees. Worth a one-line comment stating that assumption, since the predicate is the entire correctness hinge for the offset.

issues.description: Test corpus omits the `none` keyword and `calc()` channels in relative-color position.
issues.detail: Relative color syntax permits `none` and `calc(...)` as channel values. The added tests cover identifiers (`l c h`) and numbers, but not `none` or `calc()`. Not necessarily this PR's job, but worth a note so the next bug report does not surprise anyone.

review.summary: The fix is small, localized, and algorithmically correct: detect the `from` keyword, shift the channel index by 2. Complexity is unchanged (single linear scan via filter, O(n) in node count) and the data structure (filtered array of word/function nodes) is appropriate. What is missing is literate commentary stating the positional invariant the offset relies on, and a minor cleanup of `0 + offset`. Test coverage is good for the common shapes but omits `none` and `calc()` channels in relative position. Decision: RIGOROUS on the algorithm, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the invariant.
